title: dependability-bridge-sprint-kit-2026-q3
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a pragmatic sprint kit to bridge feature teams, SREs, platform, and product around a 6-week reliability push focused on service-level objectives for the serving runtime. The emphasis is cross-team, low-friction changes that materially reduce latency tail and error budget burn for client-facing generation endpoints.

High-level objectives (measurable):
- Reduce p99 generation latency by 20% for default model routes (baseline = 420ms)
- Reduce client-facing 5xx rate by 35% in the next 6 weeks
- Create guarded SLO rollout process with automated gating in CI for canary promotion
- Deliver a minimal prefix-KV cache pilot for 1 high-volume route and measure cost/token improvement

Scope (what this sprint kit covers):
- SLO definition templates and acceptance criteria
- Cross-functional tasks (instrumentation, mitigations, canary gating, runbook updates)
- Quick-win experiments and rollout plan for safe deployment
- Risk register and escalation path
- Communication cadence and owners for each artifact

Roles and RACI (short):
- Product Owner (PO): Priya Singh — owns user-impact prioritization and acceptance criteria
- SRE Lead: Ethan Wright — owns SLO enforcement, alerting, and runbook updates
- Platform/Runtime Eng: Chen Li — implements batching/cache/kernel tweaks and rollout automation
- Feature Team Liaison: Maya Rodriguez — validates end-to-end product behavior for canaries
- Program Lead / Coord: Aisha Patel — synchronizes cross-team tasks and weekly reviews

Milestones and timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): finalize SLO targets, identify 2 candidate routes, create measurement dashboards (Ethan, Chen)
- Week 1–2 (instrument + quick-wins): add histograms for sequence-length buckets, deploy client-side retry guardrails, config TTLs on caches (Chen + Feature teams)
- Week 3 (pilot deploy): roll out KV-prefix cache to route A in staging; smoke tests + load test (Maya + Chen)
- Week 4 (canary + gating): enable canary with automated abort on SLO regressions; SRE to monitor error budget burn closely (Ethan)
- Week 5 (evaluation): 72h canary window, compile metrics, cost delta, quality checks (Priya + Maya)
- Week 6 (rollout or rollback): promote to production or iterate on mitigations; update runbooks and create postmortem notes

SLO examples (templates to copy):
- Availability SLO for generation endpoints:
  "SLO": "Successful response (2xx or streaming OK) >= 99.5% over 28d",
  "Error-budget": "0.5% monthly burn threshold triggers mitigation path"
- Latency SLO for interactive routes:
  "SLO": "p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms, measured from receiving first token to last token streamed (28d rolling)"
- Model-quality guard (non-numeric but required):
  "SLO": "No regression > 3% in golden prompt eval set post-deployment (auto-run on canary)"

Acceptance criteria for canary promotion:
- No more than 10% increase in p99 vs baseline for route
- No SLO violation in 72-hour canary window
- No >1% increase in error-rate for client-facing 5xx
- Automated CI checks passed (lint + canary-promote job + eval-suite)
- Runbook updated and on-call notified in advance

Instrumentation checklist (quick):
- [ ] Per-route latency histograms by model, sequence-length bucket (Chen)
- [ ] Error classification by upstream causes (timeout, oom, infra, model) (Ethan)
- [ ] Tag traces with rollout-id and canary-flag (Platform) (Chen)
- [ ] Add golden-prompt eval in CI that runs against canary cluster (Product + QA) (Priya)

Quick-win mitigations (low-risk):
- Adaptive retry on backend shards with exponential backoff and jitter
- Request hedging for tail-prone requests (disabled by default, on canary)
- Short-circuit fallback to smaller quantized model variant on memory pressure

Experiments to run (with owners):
- Continuous batching sanity: evaluate batching window vs latency tradeoff (Chen)
- Prefix-KV caching: measure token cost reduction and hit-rate for route A (Maya)
- Dynamic kernel selection: assess p99 improvements when switching kernels for long-seq requests (Chen + Research)

Risk register (top items):
- Model quality regressions from cache/chunking — mitigations: run evals on golden set pre-promotion
- Hidden infra coupling causing canaries to pass but prod to fail — mitigations: run scaled load tests that mimic real traffic patterns
- Alert fatigue if thresholds are too sensitive — mitigations: SRE to tune and aggregate alerts into a single incident channel

Escalation path (contact order):
1. Oncall SRE (pager) -> 2. SRE Lead (Ethan) -> 3. Platform Eng (Chen) -> 4. Product PO (Priya) -> Exec Review if customer impact > high

Communication and cadence:
- Weekly cross-team sync (Wed 10:00) — review metrics, blockers, decisions (Aisha to run)
- Daily quick standup in #serving-reliability during canary windows (15 min)
- Decision doc in Confluence: link above; require +1 from SRE and Platform to promote

Artifacts to deliver by sprint end:
- Updated runbook for generation endpoints (SRE)
- Canary gating automation in CI (Platform)
- Metric dashboards and SLO burn report (SRE)
- Short retro with action items and ownership (Program Lead)

Open questions / to decide quickly:
- Which route is primary candidate for prefix-KV pilot? (suggestion: /v1/generate-beam-large)
- Acceptance threshold for golden prompt quality regressions (suggest 3%)
- Will we allow partial rollout to subset of customer accounts for extra safety?

Notes / scratchpad (informal):
- If prefix-KV hit-rate < 6% in pilot, stop and capture logs for why (likely short prompts)
- Consider adding short-circuit to local CPU fallback for tiny requests — very cheap win

Next steps (this week):
- Ethan + Chen to finalize metric list and baseline by Fri (EOD) — owners assigned in linked JIRA ENG-4882
- Maya to pick route A and assemble sample traffic replay by Mon next week
- Priya to create the canary acceptance checklist in Confluence and tag PO reviewers

Editors: Aisha Patel (program lead) — leave notes in-page; this doc intended as a lightweight operational kit for teams running service-level experiments and SLO rollouts.
